definitions.closing_reading: One reading of one message for one hearing, of a type that needs both readers because it can close a proof cell or set an official fact.
definitions.agreed: Both readers produced it for the same hearing with the same key details (it passed the cross-check).
definitions.passed: The verifier accepted it as a fact: the right sender, in writing, as a plain statement.
definitions.right: The answer key holds the same type for the same hearing with the same key details.
definitions.person_action: One of: a yes or no to one proposed proof link on the Reader suggestions tab; one proof a person types because the readers did not propose it; one message handed to a person to read; and, on the gate sheet since round 15, one cell that a person types because a rule added in round 15 reads it and the readers do not propose it (BW, AY, AZ, a later receipt pasted over the link in L, CH, CI). With auto-file on, a proposed link that is agreed and passed needs no yes; the typed cells stay with a person. A message handed to a person is counted on each hearing of its thread. This is a count of actions, not a timing.
definitions.not_counted: Typing that the method never counted, before or after round 15: the consultant's name in H, the name on the office's record in BD, a room in AV, the change notice in BN and BO, the homeowner notice in BK and BL. Messages that still have to be sent (a question to an office, a request to reply GOT IT n, a files email, a reply about an arrival time) are not counted either: they are listed for each hearing under what_remains, and one message can serve every hearing of a docket.
definitions.proofs_missing_on_the_sheet_after_this_f: What column U of the gate sheet reads once every link and typed cell above is in: one for each open check, the files check counted by its two halves. Worked out here by rules S11 and S12 from the words of the messages; cli/check.js compares it with column U of the installed sheet.

decision: Auto-file is OFF this season: nothing fills a cell on its own. The condition for switching it on is the sheet's own sentence (Reader suggestions A168): at the live-week-4 review Alice may decide that proposals both readers agree on, of one kind, fill their cell without the 9:00 pass, but only if the Friday sample found no wrong link of that kind in four weeks running. The firm's two-week log is the measurement that feeds that review; it is not a second condition. The counts in this file are from the example and unseen messages and decide nothing.
caution: The answer key was written by one person, the author of the readers' instructions. The 72 examples were used while the readers' instructions were written; the 30 unseen messages were not, and were written to be hard. Both sets are small and neither is a sample of a real mailbox. These are counts, not a policy.

sheet_examples_72.what: The 72 example messages read in order, as node cli/sheet.js does. A proof link is one message proposed as the proof for one cell (G1 to G5) of one hearing. The answer key side is the same engine fed with the answer key and no reader.

half_proofs.what: A receipt of the case files from the clerk or the consultant where the other half of G4 is still missing. The gate stays open, but the cell (Hearings L or M) can be filled.

hearings_identical_to_the_answer_key.what: Hearings whose five cells have the same status, and the same proof messages where a cell is closed, from the readers and from the answer key.
